newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks close on positive tone, gold up.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks close on positive tone, gold up.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 93.265 +0.035 Gold NY 320.05 Lon fix 320.80
AUD open $0.7455 (Tue cl $0.7439) CRB Index 232.96 +0.74
*Shares end on strong note buoyed by a bounce in the bullion price. PMP sale boosts trade. Vol 415.20 million, value A$1,042 million, 1,097 stocks traded, 273 steady, 548 up, 276 down.

Australian shares closed on a positive tone on Tuesday as gold stocks rebounded for the first time in four days and yield sensitive stocks rose on positive sentiment on interest rates ahead of Thursday's job data.
At 4.20 p.m. (0620 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 16.9 points up at 2,696.1, just off the intra-day high of 2,697.0.
The September share price index futures contract ended 15 points higher at 2,720, maintaining a premium to the underlying index of 23.9 points.
Trade was boosted by News Corp's A$325 million sale of its entire stake in magazine publisher PMP Communications.
The rise ended four days of falls following the sale of the majority of the gold reserves of Australia's central bank.

Brokers said the market could continue to make up the recent lost ground on Thursday if Wall Street hits the 8,000 level and if Australia's June jobs data is weaker than expected, which could set the scene for another interest rate cut.
Australia's battered gold sector was the strongest riser on Wednesday up over three percent. The index had lost 16 percent over the four days to Tuesday.
"They (gold sector) have found some support," said Robert Osborn, an analyst at fund managers Tyndall Australia.

The surprise sale by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp of its stake in PMP Communications was the market highlight with brokers Were Stockbroking handling the sale of A$3.20 per PMP share. Brokers were unsure if Were offloaded the stake.
"No-one quite knows whether they got rid of it," Osborn said. The sale dampened media stocks, which was one of the few sectors to go against the rising trend.

Banks and insurance stocks also performed well as investors took heart from 10-year bond futures contracts near three and a half year lows. The short-term yield has already factored in another interest rate cut.
The insurance index closed over two percent up, while banks ended over one percent higher. The Reserve Bank last cut official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent.
Investors are tipping a further cut soon and June jobs data may be a trigger. Employment is expected to rise over 40,000 for the month of June after falling by a similar amount in May.

"If there is a bad number tomorrow there could be another rate cut," Osborn said. "Although it would have to be either no growth or low positive growth and a further fall would mean a another definite cut," he said.
The Australia bond market closed firm ahead of Thursday's labour force data amid a feeling that even a very strong rebound in employment will not dent interest rate cut expectations.
At 5.05 p.m.(0705 GMT), the 10-year T-bond was four percentage points lower at 6.73 percent.
At the same time, the Australian dollar was holding off its 18 month low hit locally on Tuesday, but shed most of the offshore rally overnight in local trading.
At 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), the local dollar was at U$0.7435/40, compared with a $0.7418/23 finish here on Tuesday.
